summary: Intake one identified external literature lead as a canonical Library note and exactly one atomic terminal route: existing-node literature anchor, Frontier task, or reasoned rejection. Fully self-contained; executors need no other file.
applies_when: Conservative router: choose only when the origin issue text unambiguously requests intake and three-way triage of ONE identified external source into D5, and exactly one flow matches. POSITIVE FIXTURE: `Triage DOI 10.1000/example into a Library note as anchor, Frontier task, or rejection` => choose `library-intake-triage`. NEGATIVE FIXTURE: `Run the weekly D5 literature sweep and update queries` => choose none/plain devloop. OVERLAP FIXTURE: `Triage DOI 10.1000/example and formalize its theorem in Lean` => choose none/plain devloop because formalization is a second independently mergeable deliverable. AMBIGUOUS FIXTURE: `Review recent D5 literature` => choose none/plain devloop because it names no single source and requests no three-way triage. Also exclude broad reviews, bibliography maintenance, code features, formalization, and note-only edits. When uncertain, choose none/plain devloop.

steps.title: Record and route one literature lead

content.generator:
Read the origin issue from its source_ref and emit exactly one child issue title and body for the intake-and-triage step. The child must deliver ONE atomic, independently mergeable PR that records ONE identified external source as a structured Library note and completes exactly ONE terminal route: anchor, task, or rejected. The note and route are one transaction: never create a note in one increment and classify or act on it in another. All rules are embedded below; do NOT consult any external spec file.

SOURCE IDENTITY AND DEDUPLICATION. Verify the bibliographic facts from authoritative source metadata when available; do not invent a title, DOI, claim, license, or locator. Derive the canonical lowercase bibkey as <surname><four-digit-year><first-title-word>, matching `^[a-z]+[0-9]{4}[a-z][a-z0-9]*$`. Before editing, scan every `Library/notes/*.md` note by BOTH exact bibkey and DOI compared case-insensitively. The note address is exactly `D5/L/<bibkey>` and the path is exactly `Library/notes/<bibkey>.md`. If bibkey and DOI identify different existing notes, or the bibkey belongs to a different source, fail closed with no changes and a clear WHY; never add a suffix, alias, duplicate note, or second DOI owner. If this exact source is already fully triaged and its artifacts validate, reuse its identity and disposition, create nothing, and report a successful terminal no-op; this verified replay completes rather than blocks the origin.

STRUCTURED NOTE. Create or reconcile `Library/notes/<bibkey>.md` as strict UTF-8 without BOM or CR, with canonical YAML front matter containing exactly these seven fields: `bibkey`, `title`, `doi`, `claim`, `strata_touched`, `license`, `triage`. The path and `bibkey` must match byte-for-byte. `doi` is a bare canonical DOI or null, never a resolver URL. `claim` states only what the source supports. `strata_touched` contains only canonical repository GIDs genuinely implicated by the source. Record enough source locator, search evidence, and limitations in the note body to prevent a later rescan. The terminal `triage` value is exactly one of `anchor`, `task(D5/X_Frontier/<Name>)`, or `rejected(<concise non-empty reason>)`; it is never provisional or omitted.

DETERMINISTIC THREE-WAY ROUTE. Evaluate the routes in this precedence order so overlap cannot create two outcomes. (1) TASK wins if the source contains a concrete external result or technique that could discharge or materially attack a specifically identified repository `sorry` or existing open obligation. In the SAME PR, create or reconcile exactly one canonical `D5/X_Frontier/<Name>.lean` task target. Begin its task hint with the ordinal owner marker `source:D5/L/<bibkey>;`. If the target contains exactly one task block with that marker, preserve its permanent code; more than one is an identity collision and must fail closed. Otherwise scan every repository task block and allocate `D5-T0001` when none exist, or one greater than the numerically greatest existing `D5-T####` code, zero-padded to four digits. Never fill a gap, wrap, or reuse a code; if the maximum is `D5-T9999`, fail closed. Record difficulty, dependencies, attempts, actionable hint, and prior failure evidence, plus a formal open statement when required. Set the note to `task(D5/X_Frontier/<Name>)`; the GID must resolve, and do not also modify a Blueprint literature reference. (2) ANCHOR applies only when TASK did not: the source directly supports an existing formal declaration or typed Blueprint statement. In the SAME PR, update the canonical Blueprint `*.scribe.cs` definition for the evidenced node, using `LibraryNoteRef.Create("D5/L/<bibkey>")` and `DescribeProvenance.LiteratureAttested(...)`; this derives the ASCII, ordinal, strict-round-trip `lit/<bibkey>` anchor. Emit the deterministic Markdown projection. Keep title and DOI only in the Library note; do not copy bibliographic metadata into the Blueprint. Set the note to `anchor`, and do not create a Frontier task. (3) REJECTED applies only when neither TASK nor ANCHOR applies and the source is affirmatively irrelevant to the repository. Preserve the note and evidence, set `triage` to `rejected(<reason>)`, and make no Blueprint or Frontier change. If evidence is insufficient to distinguish these predicates, fail closed with no changes and a clear WHY rather than guessing or treating ambiguity as rejection.

EXECUTABLE ACCEPTANCE FIXTURES. The child issue must require automated fixtures over synthetic repository states, not a prose-only checklist. ANCHOR FIXTURE: an attesting source with no open-obligation attack yields one final `triage: anchor` note, one typed Blueprint anchor, and no Frontier diff. TASK-OVER-ANCHOR FIXTURE: a source that both attests a node and concretely attacks an existing open obligation yields one final `task(GID)` note, one resolvable Frontier task, and no Blueprint diff because TASK wins. REJECTED FIXTURE: an affirmatively irrelevant source yields only one final rejected note. IDENTITY-COLLISION FIXTURE: split bibkey/DOI owners or multiple owner-marked task blocks fail closed with no diff. REPLAY FIXTURE: apply each valid result twice; the second application is a successful terminal no-op with byte-identical files and no duplicate note, anchor, provenance reference, task block, task code, file, or disposition. Each fixture must assert the exact changed-path set, final triage value, and absence of every losing route.

ATOMICITY, REPLAY, AND VALIDATION. Exactly one note and exactly one disposition may result. Sort any newly added reference collections with ordinal comparison. Re-running against the same source and base must select the same bibkey, path, and disposition and must not append duplicate references, task blocks, or notes. Validate the canonical note parser, DOI uniqueness, all GID round trips and existence checks, typed Scribe construction and byte-identical emissions for ANCHOR, and the Lean/task gates for TASK. Run the executable acceptance fixtures and focused regression coverage when production code changes; TDD/tests live inside this child PR. Do not ask the child to duplicate devloop consensus, CI, PR review, or merge gates; devloop provides those. If identity is unsafe, routing is non-exclusive, or no valid initial atomic change exists, the child must produce NO changes with a clear WHY; that no-changes is fatal and blocks the origin. A verified REPLAY FIXTURE is the sole no-diff exception and completes successfully.
